title: Trémais to the minister of the Marine, cipher letter, Montréal, 6 Nov 1759, ANOM, COL C11A 104, ff.346-347v (CABAC_PIAF_60950) (catalogue 1392)

steps.what: Read the catalogue entry, PR 273 and issue 810: a partial decipherment by an outside contributor already existed (about 15% of the cipher words by our count).
LAC images fetched by curl; looked for a larger rendition (LAC variants, ANOM IIIF under 50 path variants, Héritage F-reels): none online.

C11E 10 numerical sheets e001295272 and e001295276 compared with Trémais 98 il, 108 r, 115 M. Bigot: 98 rivière/comme, 108 tion/quoique, 115 guerre/eau. Every key file in the repository tested against 22 pairs.
Roy's dossier (RAPQ 1959-60) read on BAnQ numérique: prints the instruction that gave Trémais a cipher of his own, not the table, not this letter.
Stacked and dashed numbers in the September letter are the two homophones of one unit, written together.
Clear copy ff.344-345 read in full; September cipher aligned with it slot by slot (564 slots, 168 numbers with a value, 4 conflicts left).
November letter transcribed independently (1,350 groups) and compared with issue 810: 58% exact agreement, 279 numbers undecidable.
September key applied mechanically to November: 1,131 of 1,350 groups get a value (0.838); sense appears in long runs.

Line-by-line reading with 40 values added or corrected from November (some taken from issue 810) and digits chosen among the bracket alternatives: 256 cipher words sure, 83 conjectural, 69 unread runs (reading.md).

Frozen September-only key (sha256 884d92f0...) applied to November with the first digit alternative everywhere: -2.424 log-probability per character (fr-1750-nospace) on 1,246 characters; 200 shuffled tables: best -2.617, median -3.247, none at or above the real key. Caveat: the September transcriber was given a guide list of values taken from issue 810.

Retry of every unread run and conjectural word on new 6-8x crops with the extended key, by two Claude agents (268 places: 181 sure, 64 conjectural, 23 open). The image decided no digit; gains came from recurring misreads of September numbers (32 for 92, 192 for 132, 385 for 382, 296 for 394/294/236) and new values confirmed in two places (212 dans, 233 bien, 417 un, 473 n, 402 fort, 99 dont, 195 où). Reading now 357 sure cipher words, 92 conjectural, 25 unread runs.

validation.notes: Frozen September-only key against 200 shuffled tables on November: 0 of 200 reach it (control_frozen_key.out). No reader review by a person.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Values come from the letter of 22 Sept 1759 and its contemporary decipherment in the same volume, extended from the November letter by context.
outcome.fraction_read_source: count_reading.py on reading.md: 357 sure cipher words over an estimated 472 (357 sure + 92 conjectural + about 23 words in 67 unread groups); 0.951 with the conjectural words. The total is an estimate, not the README word measure.

texts.label: ANOM, COL C11A 104, ff.346-347v
texts.summary: Trémais tells the minister that M. Bigot, however reprehensible for his 'commerce immense' and the abuses that followed, cannot justly be accused of having alone caused Canada's ills and the prodigious rise of its expenses: in the posts the military is 'absolument despote' over works, stores, provisions and rations; governor and intendant were 'fantômes' governed by Péan, Mercier and their secretaries, backed by a man raised from butcher's boy (the munitionnaire by the sense); a portrait, apparently of Montcalm, ends 'personne n'a plus contribué que lui'.

reading_review.by: Claude Fable 5.2 (a model reading, not a person)
reading_review.note: Read sentence by sentence against reading_en.md after the retry: the letter builds continuous French on f.346r and through most of ff.346v-347r; 25 short runs and 92 conjectural words remain, marked in place. No person has reviewed it.

texts.label: ANOM, COL C11A 104, ff.342-343v (22 Sept 1759), the key source
texts.summary: Trémais reports that the papers were sent to Trois-Rivières before he could use them and that he has only general talk to go on: Bigot's fortune made by trade, the troops' insatiable claims, Montcalm's demands, real but enormous consumption, no rolls, the soldier left to plunder. The text is the ministry's own decipherment, transcribed here; it supplied the key.

reading_review.by: Claude Fable 5.2 (a model reading, not a person)
reading_review.note: The contemporary clear copy, read from the images; it is continuous French throughout.
